chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fadala, from Saif, from Abu Bakr, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Take the wealth of the al-Nasib (those who oppose the Imams) wherever you find it, and pay one-fifth (khums) of it to us."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah; a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Al-Nasib; a term for those who oppose or are hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically the Imams.
key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: Its one-fifth; referring to the khums tax, a fifth of surplus wealth or specific categories of income.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the wealth of the al-Nasib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *Khums al-Nasib*, granting the Imam authority over the wealth of those who opposed the Ahl al-Bayt, a ruling derived from the concept of spoils of war or specific divine grant. It underscores the political and economic dimensions of Imamate in Shia jurisprudence, linking spiritual allegiance with material stewardship. The directive to remit one-fifth emphasizes the Imam's role as the rightful recipient of divine surplus, reinforcing the theological basis for the Imam's financial rights.
